newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips end down, small-caps up sharply.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips end down, small-caps up sharply.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip stocks ended down on Boxing Day, while small-capitalised stocks surged nearly four percent. But volumes remained stubbornly thin as several overseas bourses were closed for the seasonal break.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-cap issues was off 1.64 points to 1,207.68, while the Second Board index ended up 23.61 points to 567.23, or 4.34 percent.
"The Second Board has been very oversold recently," said Irene Tan, head of research at brokers Vickers Ballas.
The 225-share Nikkei average dropped more than 700 points or over three percent before closing down 257.38 points.

Tenaga was down 10 cents to 11.60. The company is due to hold its annual general meeting on Friday. "Everything (about Tenaga) is quite clear cut now. They are working on improving their image," said Tan.
Volume was low with 106 million shares traded, valued at 816 million ringgit. Gainers outnumbered losers 442 to 132.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot December contract was up 2.5 points to 1,196.7 on a volume of 183 lots, while the January futures contract was up 1.1 to 1,204.9 with 88 lots traded.
